title: IFR practice on the Phoenix ILS 07L

items.prompt: In the plate’s profile view, select the symbol that marks the final approach fix for the localizer approach.
items.hint: For the localizer approach, the FAF is marked with a symbol, not a step in the line.
items.explanation: The Maltese cross at ZINGA marks the localizer final approach fix. The lightning-bolt symbol identifies the ILS glideslope intercept.

items.prompt: Read the plate's profile view. What altitude is printed at ZINGA?
items.hint: In the profile view, each fix has its altitude printed just below or beside it.
items.explanation: The profile prints 2,600 ft MSL at ZINGA. The reveal turns on the map labels so you can find that altitude on the 3D route.

items.prompt: Follow the published missed approach on the plate. Which fix is named for the hold?
items.hint: The missed approach instructions end at a fix where a holding pattern is drawn.
items.explanation: The missed approach leads to the PXR VORTAC for the hold. The fixes west of the runway are on the inbound side of the procedure.

items.prompt: Read the plate's plan view. What inbound course is published for the final approach to Runway 07L?
items.hint: The course is printed along the localizer arrow in the plan view, pointing toward the runway.
items.explanation: The plan view prints 078° along the localizer course into Runway 07L. 258° is its reciprocal, the back course.
